title: Proceduralizer: Integrate admin utilities into task-driven support flows
creator: Maya Chen
description: Consolidate and modernize internal admin utilities and runbooks by building a Proceduralizer service that converts existing runbook steps into executable, observable tasks. The goal is to reduce cognitive load for on-call engineers, enable idempotent task execution, and allow support agents to trigger vetted flows via the Console, Slack ops bot, or a lightweight CLI. This ticket covers discovery, prototype, and integration with the Ops Assistant and the task queue runtime.
acceptance_criteria: A CLI tool or web UI that converts at least 10 canonical runbooks into Proceduralizer tasks and stores their definitions in the task registry
End-to-end execution of a converted runbook via Slack command and via Console action with audit logs and per-step status
Task definitions support parameter validation, secrets injection via KMS, timeout and retry policies, and idempotency keys
Observability: traces and per-step metrics emitted to Console (latency, success rate), and a dashboard template exists
Rollback: ability to disable a Proceduralizer flow and route to human-assisted fallback within 5 minutes
Security: security_review_required flag addressed and secrets flow approved by Security
plan: Discovery (2w): inventory current admin utilities, prioritize 10 high-value runbooks, interview SREs and support engineers
Spike (1w): implement minimal prototype that wraps an existing admin CLI command as a task with input schema and logging
Task Registry & Schema (1w): design JSON schema for tasks (inputs, outputs, retries, scopes) and store in shared registry
Integration (2w): wire Proceduralizer to Ops Assistant (Slack) and Console action buttons; build a lightweight CLI for devs
Observability & RBAC (1w): emit OpenTelemetry spans and add role checks for who can run flows
Rollout (1w): migrate 3 non-critical runbooks to Proceduralizer, gather feedback, iterate, then expand
